name: Socata TB 30 Epsilon
summary: French tandem two-seat primary trainer with a Lycoming flat-six and a sliding canopy, used by the French Air Force and Portugal, Togo and Tunisia; a few now fly privately.

wings: Low, tapered cantilever wing with squared-off tips
engines: Single six-cylinder Lycoming with a two-blade propeller
fuselage: Tandem seats under a long sliding bubble canopy
Slender fuselage with a smooth dorsal line
tail: Swept fin with a small dorsal fillet

tellTales: Tandem two-seater with a long bubble canopy and a low-slung, smooth fuselage
Tapered low wing with squared tips and a flat-six nose
Looks like a miniature jet trainer with a propeller

confusedWith.howToTell: The PC-7 has a turboprop nose with exhaust stacks; the Epsilon has a piston cowl and no exhaust stubs.
The T-34 has a different tail and nose with a higher canopy hump; the Epsilon has a longer canopy and a more swept fin.
The SF.260 has tip tanks and a thinner pencil-like fuselage; the Epsilon has none.
The Tucano has a turboprop nose and a ventral scoop; the Epsilon has a piston cowl.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
